slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Theorem: a tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency. Conversely, a line perpendicular to a radius at its outer endpoint is tangent.

Proof (indirect): suppose tangent t at T were not perpendicular to OT. Then the perpendicular from O to t meets t at some other point F, and OF < OT because the perpendicular is the shortest segment from a point to a line (5.3). So F is inside the circle, and line t would cross the circle twice. That contradicts t being tangent.

slides.html: A tangent from a point P touches a circle of radius 5 at T, and PO = 13. Find PT.
slides.reveal: Angle OTP is right, so PT = √(169 − 25) = 12.
